summary.text: Jon Husted is the Republican incumbent in Ohio's 2026 U.S. Senate special election, appointed by Gov. Mike DeWine in January 2025 to fill the seat vacated by J.D. Vance. A University of Dayton graduate from northwest Ohio, he worked for a county commissioner and the Dayton-area chamber of commerce before serving as Ohio House speaker, state senator, secretary of state and lieutenant governor. His campaign emphasizes his record in public office.

paragraphs.text: Husted was born in Royal Oak, Michigan, in 1967. According to his Senate office, he started life in a foster home before being adopted by Jim and Judy Husted, and he was raised in Williams County in northwest Ohio, graduating from Montpelier High School.

He earned a bachelor's degree in education in 1989 and a master's degree in communications in 1993 from the University of Dayton, where he played football; his Senate biography describes him as an All-American defensive back on the 1989 Division III national championship team.

Husted worked as a commission assistant to Montgomery County Commissioner Don Lucas from 1993 to 1997 and as a color commentator on University of Dayton football broadcasts. In 1997 he joined the Dayton Area Chamber of Commerce, where Ballotpedia lists him as director and vice president and his Senate biography as Vice President for Economic Development.

Husted won election to the Ohio House of Representatives in 2000 and served from 2001 to 2009, as Speaker from 2005 to 2009. According to his Senate office, as Speaker he led passage of a budget that included an income tax cut and created the EdChoice Scholarship.

He served in the Ohio Senate from 2009 to 2011 and as Ohio secretary of state from 2011 to 2019. As secretary of state he was the named defendant in Husted v. A. Philip Randolph Institute (2018), in which the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in favor of Ohio's process for maintaining voter rolls.

Husted then served as lieutenant governor under DeWine from 2019 to 2025 and as director of the Governor's Office of Workforce Transformation; his Senate biography credits him with the TechCred job-training program and InnovateOhio.

DeWine appointed Husted to the U.S. Senate on January 17, 2025, to replace Vance, who had become vice president. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Committees on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions; Small Business and Entrepreneurship; Environment and Public Works; and Appropriations.
According to his Senate office, he and his wife, Tina, raised three children and live in Columbus, where they attend Riverside Church.
